title: Half-Heusler LiSbZn and LiBiZn: hinge states and the archived strain models

decision_points.fork: What the archived "strained_setup" models contain. Their bct lattice vectors give c = sqrt(2) a_t = c0 and the volume of the orig cell, the Gamma8 quartet is intact, and the LiBiZn bands match the orig model to a few meV. They are the equilibrium cubic structures in a tetragonal setting, and the kwant_ham "*_strain.ham" pickles hold the same data. The archive contains no strained Hamiltonian.
decision_points.wrong_choice: Trust the file names and the paper (delta = +-2 %)
decision_points.consequence: strain +-2 % instead of 0 for both strained-setup models; LiSbZn calculation differences read as strain effects

decision_points.fork: Fundamental gap of LiSbZn from a full-zone search. The conduction-band minimum lies next to L (about 1 meV below L), not at Gamma6, so the gap is indirect.
decision_points.consequence: 352.0 and 313.0 meV instead of 343.8 and 251.7 meV

decision_points.fork: Whether LiBiZn is a zero-gap semiconductor with E_F at Gamma8, or a compensated semimetal. Band 7 near L lies 871.0 meV below the Gamma8 maximum, and E_F follows from the six-electron count (Li 1 + Zn 2 + X-p 3) on a converged mesh.
decision_points.wrong_choice: E_F at the Gamma8 touching point (half-filled quartet, as the paper describes it), or a coarse mesh
decision_points.consequence: E_F 0, -546.0 or -386.0 meV instead of -402.0 meV relative to Gamma8; gap 0 instead of -871.0 meV

decision_points.fork: Energy reference for LiSbZn. The FPLO zero sits at an arbitrary point inside the gap, and at a different point in the two LiSbZn calculations, so energies must be referred to each model's own VBM.
decision_points.wrong_choice: Use the model zero as the reference (taken as E_F)
decision_points.consequence: hinge energies 181.1 and -113.4 meV instead of 227.8 and 175.2 meV

decision_points.fork: Which hinge carries the in-gap state. In the service geometry the Zn site sits at +1/4 along both sides, so Zn is outermost on the t = N-1 facets; the state lies at the Zn/Zn hinge with about two-thirds Zn-4s weight. The paper puts it at the Bi/Sb hinge with about 95 % Bi/Sb weight. Its real-space picture is mirrored by the authors' kwant HoppingKind assignment, which reverses each hopping vector relative to the site positions.
decision_points.wrong_choice: Adopt the paper's Bi/Sb-hinge assignment and orbital character
decision_points.consequence: termination X/X and Zn-4s weight 0.05 instead of Zn/Zn and 0.68

decision_points.fork: Finite-size convergence of the k = 0 hinge level. It sits close to the conduction band and converges slowly: +7.9 meV at N = 12 and +1.2 meV at N = 20.
decision_points.wrong_choice: Read the level from a small prism (N <= 12)

decision_points.fork: Hinge-band window. The minimum is at k = pi, not k = 0. The upper of the two spin-split branches peaks near k = 1.0, inside the projected gap but far above the global conduction-band minimum.
decision_points.wrong_choice: A coarse k grid, clipping to the global gap, assuming the minimum at k = 0, or keeping one branch only

decision_points.fork: The same physical prism in the strained-setup file. Its Cartesian frame is rotated by -45 deg about z and its lattice basis differs, so P_N needs the basis [[1,0,0],[1,1,1],[1,0,1]], which puts the Zn site at reduced (1/4, 1/4, 1/4).
decision_points.wrong_choice: Reuse the orig integer basis, as the authors' shape function does in the file's own basis
decision_points.consequence: a prism with (100) and (111) facets whose gap is full of facet states; the most corner-weighted level is 205.5 meV instead of 175.2 meV

decision_points.fork: Trivial or higher-order origin. The decisive test is a local potential at the hinge that carries the state. An attractive potential of -0.38 eV on its 2x2 cells pushes the level into the valence band and pulls new bound states out of the conduction band.
decision_points.wrong_choice: Apply the test at the paper's Bi/Sb (X/X) hinge, see no effect and conclude that the state is protected
decision_points.consequence: removal potential null instead of -0.38 eV (and -0.313 eV if the level is driven to the FPLO zero instead of the VBM, dp4)

graded_fields: strain_percent of all four models within +-0.25 of 0
hinge.energy_k0_meV: LiSbZn_orig 227.8 +-6.0, LiSbZn_strained_setup 175.2 +-6.0 (relative to each VBM)

length_estimate.catalog_units: unbounded: every request is a new evaluation (bulk bands, band-edge meshes, Fermi levels, slabs, prisms of any size up to 28 with optional potentials)
length_estimate.why: Bulk classification of four models (inversion, full-zone gaps, a semimetal Fermi level), discovery that the "strained" files are cubic and use another frame, prism size convergence, assignment of the hinge from the cell geometry against the paper, a k-resolved hinge-band scan, the same prism rebuilt in the rotated file, and a potential scan; prisms of size 21-28 cost 3 units, so the 30-unit budget forces choices.

runtime_dependencies: numpy and scipy (runtime image); no extra layer
notes: Adapted from the candidate design (see the construction README). The archive holds no strained Hamiltonian: both "eq_strained_setup" files are the cubic equilibrium structures in a tetragonal setting. Strain-dependent targets were therefore replaced by what the data contain: the identification of the archived models, bulk band edges and the LiBiZn Fermi level, and the LiSbZn hinge state (assignment, converged energy, dispersion window, orbital character, removal by a local potential) in two independent LiSbZn calculations. Strong Z2 is not graded: it is trivially 0 for normal-ordered LiSbZn and undefined for cubic LiBiZn, where the Gamma8 touching is unremoved.
